Advisory.Description:
### Impact

`Schema.TemplateLiteral` compiles each `Schema.String` span to the lazy wildcard `[\s\S]*?` and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more `Schema.String` spans, for example:

```ts
Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X")
```

the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. A 5,000-character string of `:` characters blocks the event loop for about 15 seconds.

Applications that decode untrusted input with such a schema are affected. That includes `Schema.decodeUnknown`, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.is`, and anything built on them, such as `HttpApi` request payloads and `@effect/rpc` payloads.

### Patches

Fixed in `effect@3.22.1` (#6761). Template literals whose spans are all `Schema.String` are now matched with a linear left-to-right scan instead of a regular expression.

### Workarounds

If you can't upgrade, check the input length before the template literal runs. Adding `Schema.maxLength` with `.pipe` doesn't help, because the filter runs after the regex. Put the length check on the input side instead:

```ts
Schema.compose(Schema.String.pipe(Schema.maxLength(256)), MyTemplateLiteral)
```

Rejecting oversized request bodies before they reach the schema also works.
Advisory.Summary: Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex
